newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI to cut CRR by one pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI to cut CRR by one pct in Jan.

text.p: India's central bank said on Thursday it would cut the cash reserve ratio (CRR) for banks by one percent in January, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
"We stand by our earlier commitment to bring down the CRR by one percent in January 1997," it quoted Chakravarty Rangarajan, the governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), as saying.
He was addressing businessmen at a meeting at the Indian Chamber of Commerce in the India's eastern city of Calcutta.
PTI quoted Rangarajan as saying monetary policy since November 1995 had been easy rather than tight and 168.25 billion rupees released through reductions in CRR till July 1996.
He said that contrary to general expectations there was a substantial rise in bank credit and "in fact most of the people do not complain about lack of lendable resources".
The banks' deposit growth continued to be strong, Rangarajan said and the economic situation would compel them to offer loans to industry, PTI added.
